title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
关于著者
莫妮卡·非特1951年生于德国哈根市。她的老师描述说，莫妮卡自小就是个爱做梦的女孩，并拥有太多的想象力，所以她得寻找一个可以让她实现这两种能力的职业。文学硕士毕业之后，她的第一份工作是记者，并曾参与儿童刊物的编辑工作。目前莫妮卡·非特是一位隐居在小村庄的自由作家，她的文字清新婉约，作品曾被译为英、法、西、日等多种语言，在各地出版。小说《我怎么啦？》曾获1991年德国电视二台书迷奖，绘本《通过图片的道路》为1992年苏黎世“La vache qui lit”文学奖的提名作品，绘本《收集思想的人》入围1994年哈默尔恩市捕鼠人文学奖和尼伦施皮格尔奖，《蓝色和灰色日子》获得北莱因-威斯特法伦州作者奖学金，并荣登银笔推荐榜。
此外，《蓝姑娘》于2001年荣登萨尔州广播台和不来梅广播台图书推荐榜并获得2002天主教儿童及青少年图书奖；《摘草莓的人》获汉斯约尔格·马丁奖提名；《鲨鸟飞》获得法国“Tam Tam du livre de jeunesse”奖；《爷爷，我可以驯服野蜂了》获得2007年弗尔卡赫市德国儿童及青少年文学学院大奖四月图书奖项以及《时代》杂志卢克斯评审团的推荐；《少女画家》获得2007年法国“Longlist vertalingen van de Boekenleeuw”大奖；《碎片收集者》获2008年布克斯特胡德公牛奖提名。
莫妮卡·非特用诗般的故事赋予我们一种新的眼光，让成人读者透过她人生的体验，重新看待世界；让小读者记取一个故事，在未来的日子里，等待发芽。
书，孩子成长的必需品。
page_text_en:
About the Author
Monika Fett was born in Hagen, Germany, in 1951. Her teacher described her as a girl who loved to dream and had a great deal of imagination, so she sought a career that could fulfill both of these abilities. After earning a master's degree in literature, her first job was as a journalist, and she also worked on editing children's publications. Currently, Monika Fett is a freelance writer living quietly in a small village. Her writing is fresh and graceful, and her works have been translated into English, French, Spanish, Japanese, and other languages, published worldwide. Her novel 'What's Wrong with Me?' won the 1991 German TV Channel 2 Book Lover Award; her picture book 'Through the Path of Pictures' was a nominee for the 1992 Zurich 'La vache qui lit' Literary Award; her picture book 'The Collector of Thoughts' was shortlisted for the 1994 Hameln Pied Piper Literary Award and the Nierenschpigel Award; and 'Blue and Gray Days' won the North Rhine-Westphalia Author Scholarship and was featured on the Silver Pen Recommendation List.
In addition, 'Blue Girl' was featured on the Saarland and Bremen radio book recommendation lists in 2001 and won the 2002 Catholic Children's and Youth Book Award; 'The Strawberry Picker' was nominated for the Hans Jörg Martin Award; 'Shark Bird Fly' won the French 'Tam Tam du livre de jeunesse' Award; 'Grandpa, I Can Tame Wild Bees' won the 2007 Fürth German Children's and Youth Literature Academy April Book Award and was recommended by the Lucks jury of 'Die Zeit' magazine; 'The Girl Painter' won the 2007 French 'Longlist vertalingen van de Boekenleeuw' Award; and 'The Fragment Collector' was nominated for the 2008 Buxtehude Bull Award.
Monika Fett uses poetic stories to give us a new perspective, allowing adult readers to re-examine the world through her life experiences, and enabling young readers to remember a story, waiting to sprout in the days to come.
Books are essential for children's growth.
summary_zh: 本页为绘本《擦亮路牌的人》的作者介绍页，详细介绍了作者莫妮卡·非特的生平、创作经历、主要作品及所获荣誉，并附有对作者文学风格的评价和一句关于阅读的寄语。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
我认识一个人，他的职业是擦洗路牌。他每天早上七点离开家，大约一个半小时后到达威豪广场上的路牌清洗中心。隔着玻璃，他向门卫问好，走进更衣室。
穿上蓝色工作服和蓝色橡胶高筒靴之后，他就到对面的库房里，在接待台领一把蓝色的梯子、一只蓝色的水桶、一把蓝色的刷子和一条蓝色的皮围裙。
他一边准备着，一边和也在做准备的同事们闲聊着。随后，他们在隔壁车库里推出各自的蓝色自行车，蹬车驶出大门。
当全城所有路牌清洗工同时出发时，那情景看上去很是壮观，就像是一大群蓝色的鸟刚飞出巢那样。
page_text_en:
I know a person whose job is to clean street signs. He leaves home every morning at seven o'clock, and after about an hour and a half, arrives at the street sign cleaning center in Weihao Square. Through the glass, he greets the guard and walks into the changing room.
After putting on his blue work clothes and blue rubber boots, he goes to the warehouse across the way, where he collects a blue ladder, a blue bucket, a blue brush, and a blue leather apron at the reception desk.
As he prepares, he chats with his colleagues who are also getting ready. Then, they push out their individual blue bicycles from the adjacent garage and pedal out the gate.
When all the street sign cleaners in the city set off at the same time, the scene is quite spectacular, like a large flock of blue birds just flying out of their nest.
summary_zh: 本页文字介绍了主角作为路牌清洗工的日常工作流程，包括早晨出发、换装、领取工具以及与同事一同骑车出发的场景，右侧插图展示了一位穿着蓝色工作服、骑着蓝色自行车的工人正从门内驶出。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
这位路牌清洗工干活儿的路线多年来一直没有变过。
他所负责的街区，大街小巷都是以诗人和音乐家的名字命名的，比如：巴赫大街、贝多芬大街、海顿大街、莫扎特小巷、格鲁克大街、瓦格纳大街、亨德尔路、肖邦广场、歌德大街、席勒大街、布莱希特小巷、凯斯特纳大街、英格博格·巴赫曼大道、最后是威廉·布什广场。当他走完这条线路，一天的工作就结束了。
清洗路牌可不是个简单的活儿。一个牌子刚被擦干净，很快又脏了。但一位出色的清洗工是不会因此而失去勇气和信心的，也不会放弃与不洁做斗争。我讲的这位清洗工就是这样一位出色和勤奋的清洗工。他所负责的街道，路牌不仅干净，而且保持得像新的一样。同事们常毫不嫉妒地称赞他是这个城市最棒的路牌清洗工。清洗工的大领导和班长也都拍着他的肩膀称赞：“好样的，继续干！”
page_text_en:
The route this street sign cleaner follows has remained unchanged for years.
He is responsible for a district where streets and alleys are named after poets and musicians, such as: Bach Street, Beethoven Street, Haydn Street, Mozart Alley, Gluck Street, Wagner Street, Handel Road, Chopin Square, Goethe Street, Schiller Street, Brecht Alley,凯斯特纳 Street, Ingeborg Bachmann Avenue, and finally William Busch Square. When he finishes this route, his day's work is done.
Cleaning street signs is no easy job. A sign is just cleaned, and soon it's dirty again. But an excellent cleaner never loses courage or confidence, nor gives up the fight against dirt. The cleaner I'm telling you about is just such an excellent and diligent worker. The signs on his streets are not only clean, but kept as good as new. His colleagues often praise him without jealousy as the city's best street sign cleaner. Even the head supervisor and team leader pat him on the shoulder and say, "Well done, keep it up!"
summary_zh: 本页介绍了路牌清洗工固定的清洁路线，该路线覆盖了以多位著名诗人和音乐家命名的街道，并强调了他工作认真、勤奋，受到同事和领导的高度赞扬。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
这个路牌清洗工十分幸福。他热爱自己的职业，热爱他的街道和牌子。如果有人问起，他希望自己的生活有哪些变化，他会说：“不需要变化。”如果不是有一天，一位妈妈带着她的孩子在他的蓝梯子旁停下脚，清洗工的生活也许会一切照旧。
“瞧，这‘格鲁克（GLUCK）大街’应该叫‘幸福（GLUCK——德语“幸福”之意）大街’！”那孩子指着清洗工正在擦洗的那个路牌子喊了起来，“是他把字上的两个小点给擦掉了。”
“哪两个点？”妈妈一边问，一边惊讶地抬起头看着。
“就是字母U上的点。”孩子回答。
“不，”妈妈笑着说，“这街名是对的。格鲁克是一个作曲家，是他发明了音乐的旋律，所以这街道用了他的名字。”
这时，一辆大巴车和两辆载重卡车正好轰轰驶过，把妈妈的话淹没了。当周围又恢复平静时，妈妈和那孩子已经走远了。
page_text_en:
This street sign cleaner is very happy. He loves his job, his streets, and his signs. If someone asks him what changes he would like in his life, he says, "No changes needed." If not for one day, when a mother and her child stopped by his blue ladder, the cleaner's life might have continued as usual.
"Look, this 'Gluck (GLUCK) Street' should be called 'Happiness (GLUCK—German for 'happiness') Street!'" the child shouted, pointing at the sign the cleaner was washing, "He erased the two little dots on the letter!"
"Which two dots?" the mother asked, looking up in surprise.
"The dots on the letter U," the child replied.
"No," the mother smiled, "The street name is correct. Gluck was a composer; he invented the melody of music, so the street is named after him."
At that moment, a bus and two heavy trucks roared by, drowning out the mother's words. When the surroundings quieted again, the mother and child had already walked away.
summary_zh: 本页描绘了一位路牌清洗工在擦拭标有“GLUCK”的路牌时，一位母亲和孩子路过并讨论路牌名称的含义。孩子认为“GLUCK”应译为“幸福”，并指出清洗工擦掉了字母U上的点；母亲则解释“格鲁克”是作曲家，街道以他命名。最后，车辆驶过，母子离开，对话中断。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
清洗工呆呆地注视着那个路牌。他突然意识到，他和
那孩子一样，对这位叫格鲁克的作曲家一无所知。这些著
名人物的名字每天都出现在他的眼前，可是他对他们几乎
没有什么了解。
这可不行，他暗自想。
他爬上梯子，从裤兜里掏出一枚一马克的硬币，向空
中抛去：雄鹰朝上，就从音乐家开始；数字朝上，就从诗
人开始。
硬币落到了台阶上，弹跳翻转，闪着光，最后停了
下来。
是雄鹰。
清洗工弯下腰，捡起硬币，在手里不停地转动，考虑
自己该做什么。他第一次希望早点儿下班。
刚到五点，他就骑上自行车，飞快地冲向路牌清洗中
心。一到中心，他就急忙换好衣服，回家去。
page_text_en:
The cleaner stared blankly at the street sign. He suddenly realized, just like the child, he knew nothing about this composer named Gluck. These famous names appeared before his eyes every day, yet he knew almost nothing about them.
This won’t do, he thought to himself.
He climbed the ladder, pulled out a one-mark coin from his pocket, and tossed it into the air: if the eagle faced up, he’d start with musicians; if the number faced up, he’d start with poets.
The coin landed on the steps, bouncing and spinning, gleaming, and finally came to a stop.
It was the eagle.
The cleaner bent down, picked up the coin, and kept turning it in his hand, thinking about what he should do. For the first time, he wished he could go home early.
Just as it was five o’clock, he jumped on his bicycle and raced toward the street sign cleaning center. As soon as he arrived, he hurriedly changed into his clothes and went home.
summary_zh: 清洗工在擦拭路牌时，意识到自己对著名人物如格鲁克一无所知，内心产生困惑。他通过抛硬币决定从音乐家开始清洁，最终硬币显示“雄鹰”，他决定从音乐家开始。他思考工作内容，希望早点下班，随后在五点骑车返回清洗中心并换好衣服回家。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
进屋关上门，他找来纸和笔，列出了一个长长的名单：巴赫——贝多芬——肖邦——格鲁克——亨德尔——海顿——莫扎特——瓦格纳。他把名单读了一遍，就用图钉固定在墙上。
然后他仔细阅读报纸，特别关注音乐会和歌剧的信息。他抄下节目单，做出计划表，把计划表放进包里。
第二天，他先买了门票，又从箱子里找出整洁的西装。“现在我知道自己缺少什么了。”每当他坐在音乐厅或歌剧院里，感受到周围那种安静得近乎紧张的氛围时，脑海里就会冒出这个念头。
音乐开始时的旋律都比较刚烈，然后柔和，随之变得丰满，接着分散开来，又汇合到一起，融合、震颤、收缩、洪亮，最后逐渐消失。清洗工颤抖着从他的音乐教育中醒了过来。纸张的沙沙声，脚步的挪动声——大门打开了，人们争先恐后地挤出去。清洗工环顾四周，不禁微笑起来。
巴赫
贝多芬
肖邦
格鲁克
亨德尔
海顿
莫扎特
瓦格纳
page_text_en:
He closed the door behind him, found paper and a pen, and made a long list: Bach—Beethoven—Chopin—Gluck—Handel—Haydn—Mozart—Wagner. He read the list aloud once, then pinned it to the wall with a thumbtack.
Then he carefully read the newspaper, paying special attention to information about concerts and operas. He copied down the program, made a schedule, and put the schedule in his bag.
The next day, he bought tickets first, then took out a neat suit from his box. “Now I know what I’m missing.” Whenever he sat in a concert hall or opera house, feeling the quiet, almost tense atmosphere around him, this thought would pop into his mind.
The melodies at the beginning of the music were usually fierce, then softened, then became full-bodied, then scattered, then came together again, merging, trembling, contracting, swelling, and finally fading away. The cleaning worker trembled as he woke up from his music education. The rustling of paper, the shuffling of feet—the door opened, and people rushed out one after another. The cleaning worker looked around and couldn’t help but smile.
Bach
Beethoven
Chopin
Gluck
Handel
Haydn
Mozart
Wagner
summary_zh: 主角在家中列出著名音乐家名单并将其钉在墙上，随后阅读报纸规划音乐会行程，第二天穿着整洁西装前往音乐厅，在音乐会结束后感到满足并微笑。右侧插图展示他坐在橙色扶手椅上阅读报纸，旁边贴着音乐家名单。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
圣诞节，他送给自己一个唱片机。打开包装，把唱片机放到圣诞树下，他高兴地放进一张唱片。
从那，每个夜晚，他都坐在客厅，听音乐。他慢慢地感觉到，那些很久前逝去的音乐家现在又复活了，成为他最好的朋友。听着他们的音乐，在思考中寻找着问题的答案，就好像在和他们聊天。
干活儿时，他轻轻地吹起已经学会的旋律——莫扎特的《小夜曲》和贝多芬的《月光奏鸣曲》。他甚至可以熟练地吹歌剧了。这可不容易，因为他只能吹出一个声音，而歌剧中的其他声音他必须用想象来完成。
当他熟悉了名单上的所有音乐家之后，就把名单从墙上取下来，把纸翻过来，在上面又写下一份诗人名单：
巴赫曼——布莱希特——威廉·布什——歌德——格利帕泽——凯斯特纳——托马斯·曼——席勒——斯托姆。
他把新名单挂在墙上，然后去城市的图书馆借阅这些作家们的作品。
page_text_en:
On Christmas, he gave himself a record player. He opened the package, placed the record player under the Christmas tree, and happily put in a record.
From then on, every night, he sat in the living room, listening to music. He slowly felt that the musicians who had passed away long ago had come back to life, becoming his best friends. Listening to their music, he searched for answers to his questions in thought, as if chatting with them.
While working, he softly whistled melodies he had already learned—Mozart's 'Eine kleine Nachtmusik' and Beethoven's 'Moonlight Sonata'. He could even skillfully whistle operas. This was no easy feat, since he could only produce one sound, and the other sounds in the opera had to be imagined.
After becoming familiar with all the musicians on the list, he took the list down from the wall, flipped the paper over, and wrote a new list of poets: Bachmann—Brecht—Wilhelm Busch—Goethe—Griepenkerl—Kästner—Thomas Mann—Schiller—Storm.
He hung the new list on the wall, then went to the city library to borrow works by these writers.
summary_zh: 主角在圣诞节收到唱片机后，每晚聆听音乐，与逝去的音乐家‘对话’，并用口哨演奏乐曲。熟悉音乐家后，他将名单翻面，写下诗人名单，并计划去图书馆借阅这些作家的作品。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
几周后，图书管理员已经认识他了，一见到他，就对他友好地点头。他也成为了图书馆最努力的读者。
读书时，清洗工遇到一些他过去从没有听过的文字。
有些他能够理解，有些根本不懂。不懂的地方他就反复琢磨，直到弄明白那些文字的真正含义。
一个又一个深夜，他沉浸在作品里。在故事中，他发现的秘密与他在音乐中发现的十分近似。文字是写出来的音乐，他想，或者说，也许音乐是没有说出来的文字的声音。
page_text_en:
A few weeks later, the librarian had already recognized him. When she saw him, she nodded at him warmly. He had become the most diligent reader in the library.
While reading, the cleaner encountered some words he had never heard before.
Some he could understand, others he simply didn't grasp. For the parts he didn't understand, he would ponder repeatedly until he fully grasped their true meaning.
Night after night, he immersed himself in the works. In the stories, he discovered secrets that were very similar to those he had found in music. Words are music written down, he thought, or perhaps, music is sound that hasn't been spoken.
summary_zh: 清洗工在图书馆阅读时，逐渐理解了陌生文字，并在深夜沉浸于书籍中，他感悟到文字与音乐的相似性，认为文字是写出来的音乐，音乐是未说出口的文字的声音。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
“真遗憾，”他对同事们说，“没能更早点儿就开始读书，现在才明白。”
书中的文字使他时而沉默无语，时而激动不已；让他深思熟虑，也给了他勇气、快乐和悲伤。作家用他们的文字进行表演，就像音乐家用声音、年轻人用球、或者魔术师用头巾进行表演一样。
清洗工和作家们的关系就像当初他与音乐家的关系一样——他和他们成了好朋友。
当他熟悉了所有的作品，就会在工作时背诵出自己特别喜欢的段落，比如：歌德《魔王》中的“是谁在黑夜和风中奔驰”，布莱希特的《尖刀麦基之歌》中的“龇牙咧嘴的鲨鱼”，斯托姆的《骑白马的怪神》和威廉·布什的《马克斯和莫里茨》。
page_text_en:
"What a pity," he said to his colleagues, "I wish I had started reading sooner. I understand now." 
 The words in the books made him sometimes silent, sometimes deeply moved; they made him think deeply and gave him courage, joy, and sorrow. Writers perform with their words, just as musicians perform with sound, young people with balls, or magicians with scarves. 
 The cleaner's relationship with the writers was just like his earlier relationship with the musicians—he had become good friends with them. 
 When he became familiar with all the works, he would recite his favorite passages while working, such as: Goethe's 'The Erlking' with its line 'Who rides so late through night and wind?', Brecht's 'The Song of the Knife-McGee' with its line 'The grinning shark', Storm's 'The Strange Rider on the White Horse', and Wilhelm Busch's 'Max and Moritz'.
summary_zh: 清洗工在阅读书籍后深受触动，他将作家与音乐家类比，认为文字如同表演，并与作家们建立了深厚的情感联系。他开始在工作中背诵喜爱的文学段落，如歌德、布莱希特、斯托姆和威廉·布什的作品。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
就这样，在清洗路牌时，他吹着口哨、背诵诗歌、唱着歌曲、讲着故事。
行人们停下来听他说明。他们注视着那蓝色的梯子，惊讶无比。他们还从没有遇到过这样一位清洗工。大多数人原本以为，有的人就是清洗路牌的，有的人就是从事诗歌、音乐工作的。他们称前者为工人，后者为受过教育的文化人。现在居然有人同时做两件事情，这大大超出了他们的想象。他们原本的想法被推翻了。
page_text_en:
This way, while cleaning street signs, he whistled, recited poetry, sang songs, and told stories.
Passersby stopped to listen to him. They stared at the blue ladder, amazed. They had never encountered such a cleaner before. Most people originally thought that some people were just street sign cleaners, while others were engaged in poetry and music. They called the former workers and the latter educated cultural figures. Now, someone was doing both at the same time, which greatly exceeded their imagination. Their original ideas were overturned.
summary_zh: 清洗工在清洗路牌时吹口哨、背诗、唱歌、讲故事，行人们停下来看他，惊讶于一个工人能同时从事文化活动，颠覆了他们对职业的刻板印象。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
但站在梯子上的清洗工根本没注意到大家对他的敬佩。他只顾清洗并擦亮那些路牌，直到一尘不染的路牌在太阳下闪闪发光为止。
下班后，他去图书馆借阅有关那些音乐家和作家作品的评论。这些作品很难理解，有时他觉得永远都读不懂。
时间过得很快，当他把所有重要的作品读完后，已经快老了。但他仍然一如既往地爱惜和清洗着那些路牌，还时常用指尖抚摸着那些让他刻骨铭心的名字。有时，他还边工作边自言自语地对音乐和文学作品做着评论。
page_text_en:
But the cleaner standing on the ladder didn't notice everyone's admiration. He only focused on cleaning and polishing the street signs until they shone spotlessly in the sun.
After work, he went to the library to borrow reviews about the works of those musicians and writers. These works were hard to understand, and sometimes he felt he would never be able to comprehend them.
Time passed quickly, and when he had finished reading all the important works, he was nearly old. But he still continued to cherish and clean those street signs, often gently touching with his fingertips the names that had become deeply engraved in his heart. Sometimes, he would comment aloud on music and literature while working.
summary_zh: 清洗工专注于清洗路牌，未察觉他人敬佩的目光；下班后他借阅音乐家和作家作品的评论，虽感难懂却坚持阅读，晚年仍保持对艺术的热爱，并在工作中自言自语评论作品。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
一天，一家人经过他的梯子，驻足倾听。两个过路的小女孩不再聊天，抬头看着他。还有一个小伙子放下书包，认真地听起来。一个班级的学生和老师也一起围了过来。其他行人看到有人聚在一起，也围了过来。
清洗工却没注意到这些，仍然继续自言自语。当他把路牌清洗干净，从蓝色梯子上下来时，大家鼓起掌来。清洗工的脸一下子涨得通红。他赶紧收拾好工具，推着蓝色的自行车向下一个路牌走去。
人们跟着他。虽然这对一个清洗工来说不太合适，但他又能怎么办呢？总不能让他们跟着呀。他只好继续工作，接着做评论，并且努力不朝下看。
page_text_en:
One day, a family passed by his ladder and stopped to listen. Two little girls passing by stopped chatting and looked up at him. A young man put down his backpack and listened attentively. A class of students and their teacher also gathered around. Other pedestrians, seeing the crowd, joined in too.

The cleaner didn't notice any of this and continued talking to himself. When he finished cleaning the sign and stepped down from the blue ladder, everyone clapped. The cleaner's face turned bright red. He quickly gathered his tools and pushed his blue bicycle toward the next sign.

People followed him. Although it was a bit inappropriate for a cleaner, what else could he do? He couldn't let them follow him, after all. So he continued working, kept making comments, and tried not to look down.
summary_zh: 清洗工在工作时自言自语，吸引了路人驻足倾听，甚至有人鼓掌。他并未察觉，只顾继续工作，但人们开始跟随他，他只能继续工作并努力不低头看。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
时间一小时一小时地过去了。当威豪广场教堂上的时钟终于指到下午五点时，清洗工轻快地骑车离去，听众们在他的身后频频招手示意。
第二天一早，听众们已经在巴赫大街等他了。清洗工打了一个响嗝，屏住呼吸，慢慢地数到十，然后把蓝梯子在第一个路牌下打开，开始清洗路牌和做新的评论报告。人们踮着脚尖围着他倾听。当他擦净最后一块路牌，讲完最后一句话，人群里发出一阵赞许声。他害羞地匆忙跑开后，听众才四散而去。清洗工这时突然明白，从现在开始，他要面对公众了。他应该在出场前做好准备，不能给自己丢脸。
前来听报告的人越来越多，蓝色梯子前也越来越拥挤。渐渐地，清洗工习惯了他的听众。他从一块路牌到另一块路牌，用梯子爬上爬下，不再受周围的影响。
page_text_en:
Time passed hour by hour. When the clock at the Weihao Square church finally struck five in the afternoon, the cleaner rode away cheerfully, and the audience waved goodbye behind him.
Early the next morning, the audience was already waiting for him on Bach Street. The cleaner let out a loud belch, held his breath, slowly counted to ten, then unfolded the blue ladder under the first street sign, beginning to clean the signs and deliver his new commentary report. People stood on tiptoe around him, listening. When he finished cleaning the last sign and delivered his final words, the crowd burst into applause. Embarrassed, he hurried away, and only then did the audience disperse. The cleaner suddenly realized that from now on, he would be facing the public. He should prepare himself before appearing, and not embarrass himself.
More and more people came to listen to his reports, and the area around the blue ladder became increasingly crowded. Gradually, the cleaner grew accustomed to his audience. He moved from one sign to another, climbing up and down the ladder, no longer affected by his surroundings.
summary_zh: 清洗工在完成一天工作后离开，第二天清晨已有听众在街边等候。他开始在清洗路牌时进行评论，引来人群围观并获得掌声。他逐渐习惯公众关注，不再受周围影响，继续专注工作。

title_en: The Person Who Wipes the Sign
page_text_ocr_zh:
一天，来了许多摄影师，还有一位电视台《与你和我一样的人》栏目的记者，他们给正在干活的清洗工录像摄影，还采访了他。
他一夜之间成了名人。
大家都在讲述着他的故事。索要他签名的人把他团团围住。他收到一袋又一袋的来信。路牌清洗中心的领导和作业班长对他说了一堆故作庄重的话，还送他一束鲜花。
由于他的缘故，路牌清洗中心在社会上的地位得到很大提高。多所大学邀请他去做报告。清洗工如果接受邀请，可以得到令人羡慕的发展。
清洗工没有这么做。
“我只是一个普普通通的人。”他在回信中写道，“我每天最爱做的就是清洗路牌。我做报告只是为了自己，为了快乐和消遣。我不想做教授。我离不开我的工作。顺致崇高的敬意。”
就这样，他还是他，一个路牌清洗工。
page_text_en:
One day, many photographers arrived, along with a reporter from the TV show 'You and I, the Same People.' They filmed and interviewed the cleaning worker while he was working.
He became famous overnight.
Everyone was telling his story. People surrounded him to get his autograph. He received bag after bag of letters. The leaders and team supervisors at the sign-cleaning center said a lot of solemn-sounding words to him and even gave him a bouquet of flowers.
Because of him, the sign-cleaning center's status in society greatly improved. Several universities invited him to give lectures. If the cleaning worker accepted the invitations, he could achieve a desirable future.
But the cleaning worker didn't do that.
'I am just an ordinary person,' he wrote in his reply. 'What I love most every day is cleaning signs. I give lectures only for myself, for joy and amusement. I don't want to be a professor. I can't leave my job. With highest regards.'
And so, he remained himself, a sign-cleaning worker.
summary_zh: 清洗工因在工作中背诵文学作品而受到媒体关注，一夜成名，收到大量信件和邀请，但他拒绝了所有邀约，坚持做一名普通的路牌清洗工。

关于绘者
安图尼·波阿提里思克1930年出生于波兰巴沃里，在华沙和
布达佩斯的学院攻读美术。自19世纪60年代起就开始创作图画
书，但一直到80年代一些西欧出版社发现他的作品后，才受到广
泛的关注。目前从事艺术创作及插画工作，画作在波兰及许多国
际展览中展出。曾获得欧洲波米欧奖、布拉迪斯拉发金苹果奖，
亦曾入围国际安徒生奖。他的作品色彩沉静，意境悠远，用超现
实主义的手法表达视觉上无法理解的东西，赋予读者无限的想象
空间。
安图尼·波阿提里思克与擅长以幽默恬静、富有诗意的文字
来描绘心中理想故事的莫妮卡·菲特合作的故事——《收集思想
的人》《擦亮路牌的人》《画家、城市和大海》与《当颜色被禁止
的时候》，都带有耐人寻味的哲学思维，不只适合亲子共读，更
适合所有成人细细咀嚼，用心品味他们笔下的世界，以新的视野
看待生命与我们所处的社会。
这四部作品已被翻译成十八种语言，其中三部被改编成电影。
《收集思想的人》荣获捕鼠人文学奖和猫头鹰文学奖提名奖；《擦
亮路牌的人》荣获德国青少年科学奖，该书被德国国家图书馆
授予收入德国国家图书目录资格荣誉，并在指定网站提供浏览。

About the Illustrator
Antoni Piotrowski was born in 1930 in Bawory, Poland, and studied art at academies in Warsaw and Budapest. He began creating picture books in the 1960s, but it wasn't until the 1980s, when some Western European publishers discovered his work, that he gained widespread attention. He currently engages in artistic creation and illustration, with his artworks exhibited in Poland and many international exhibitions. He has won the European Bomiou Award and the Bratislava Golden Apple Award, and has also been shortlisted for the Hans Christian Andersen Award. His works feature calm colors and distant moods, using surrealistic techniques to express things visually incomprehensible, offering readers infinite imaginative space.
Antoni Piotrowski collaborated with Monica Fitt, who is skilled in using humorous, serene, and poetic texts to depict ideal stories in her heart—the stories 《The Collector of Thoughts》, 《The Man Who Polishes Signboards》, 《The Painter, the City, and the Sea》, and 《When Colors Were Banned》—all carry thought-provoking philosophical insights, suitable not only for parent-child reading but also for adults to savor carefully, to appreciate their world with a new perspective, and to view life and our society anew.
These four works have been translated into eighteen languages, with three adapted into films.
《The Collector of Thoughts》 received nominations for the Mouse Trap Literature Award and the Owl Literature Award; 《The Man Who Polishes Signboards》 won the German Youth Science Award, and the book was granted the honor of being included in the German National Library's catalog, with access available on designated websites.
summary_zh: 本页为绘本的‘关于绘者’介绍，详细说明了插画师安图尼·波阿提里思克的生平、艺术成就、创作风格，以及他与作家莫妮卡·菲特合作的四部作品的影响力和所获荣誉。
